title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). E is an elliptic curve over a field k with char k ≠ 2, and 0_E is its origin. F_n = Γ(E, O_E(n·0_E)) is the space of functions with a pole of order at most n at the origin, so F_* is a filtered commutative algebra. Grothendieck calls it 'graded', though strictly it is filtered (or the Rees algebra). Further notation:
- t_E is the tangent space at 0. Each δ ∈ t_E gives an invariant vector field and hence a derivation θ_δ : F_n → F_{n+1}.
- δ_n : t_E ⊗ F_n → F_{n+1} is the intrinsic version of θ.
- f ↦ f̌, with f̌(x) = f(−x), is the involution v induced by [−1].

What this page does.
- (15) The inversion [−1] acts by −1 on t_E, so δ̌ = −δ. Hence (θ_δ f)ˇ = θ_{δ̌} f̌ = −θ_δ f̌, i.e. v∘θ_δ = −θ_δ∘v.
- (16) Define the even part F_n^+ and the odd part F_n^- as the ±1-eigenspaces of v. Since char ≠ 2, (17) gives F_n = F_n^+ ⊕ F_n^-.
- θ_δ and δ_n exchange parity.
- Multiplication respects the Z/2-grading: (+)(+) ⊂ (+), (−)(−) ⊂ (+), (+)(−) ⊂ (−).
- Programme: describe intrinsically the filtered algebra F_* together with the map t_E → Der_k^{+1}(F_*, F_*) (equivalently δ_*) and the involution ∨ (an automorphism of order 2).
- (18) F_2 = F_2^+, since L(2·0) = ⟨1, ℘⟩ consists of even functions. F_2 ≅ Γ(Σ_J, O(t)), where:
  - Σ_J ≅ E/{±1} ≅ P^1;
  - J = ₂E^* is the set of three nonzero 2-torsion points (or their images);
  - t is the image of 0_E;
  - Σ_J^* = Σ_J ∖ J.
  Concretely, even functions with a pole of order ≤ 2n at 0 are exactly the functions on the quotient P^1 with a pole of order ≤ n at t.

Next page. Here x = ℘ and p' = θ_δ p ~ ℘′ is odd and vanishes on J, leading to the bases {p^i} and {p′p^i}.

In short, this page is an intrinsic, coordinate-free set-up of the Weierstrass/Legendre description of E as a double cover of P^1 branched at t and at the three points of J. It serves the 'modules of elliptic curves in char ≠ 2' project, i.e. the moduli of elliptic curves with level-2 data via Legendre-type normal forms.
errors: In (17) Grothendieck writes t_E⊗F_n^+ →δ_n→ F_n^- and t_E⊗F_n^- → F_n^+. Since δ_n : t_E⊗F_n → F_{n+1}, the targets should be F_{n+1}^- and F_{n+1}^+. This is an index slip, harmless.
Calling F_* a 'graded algebra' is loose. It is a filtered algebra; the parity decomposition gives a genuine Z/2-grading.

ideas.what: Invariant derivation θ_δ anticommutes with the inversion involution, because [−1] acts by −1 on t_E
ideas.modern_name: Parity of ℘ and ℘′; [−1]-equivariance of invariant differentials and vector fields

ideas.what: Decomposition of the Riemann–Roch spaces L(n·0) into even and odd parts, with multiplicative Z/2-grading
ideas.modern_name: Even/odd functions; E → E/{±1} ≅ P^1 as a double cover

ideas.what: F_{2n}^+ ≅ Γ(P^1, O(n·t)), with P^1 = E/±1 marked by the image t of 0 and the three nonzero 2-torsion images J
ideas.modern_name: Kummer line / Legendre form; level-2 structure via branch points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Legendre, Weierstrass); Katz–Mazur for the moduli treatment

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful coordinate-free rederivation of the classical Weierstrass/Legendre structure (even/odd functions, ℘ and ℘′, E/±1 ≅ P^1). It is standard material in Katz–Mazur style treatments; nothing new beyond Grothendieck's personal intrinsic formulation.
transcription_corrections: In (17), the image (and transcription) gives the targets of δ_n as F_n^∓. Mathematically they should be F_{n+1}^∓; worth flagging as Grothendieck's slip.
The marginal note under (18) reads roughly 't image de 0_E et Σ_J^* = Σ_J ∖ J'. J = ₂E^* most plausibly denotes the nonzero 2-torsion points, consistent with Proposition 1 on the next page.
